question: Do surprise onside kicks get recovered more than expected late-game onside kicks?
answer: Yes, 25% against 9% (2015-23), but that is below the ~32% break-even for an early onside. Net WPA isn't different from zero.
findings: Surprise onsides were recovered 25.0% of the time (15.5-37.7, n=56), and expected ones 8.9% (6.7-11.6, n=508).
On a Q1-Q3 surprise onside, the kicking team's WPA is -0.6 points (-1.8 to +0.6, n=54). A normal kickoff is -0.04.
The break-even recovery rate for a Q1-Q3 surprise onside is about 32%.
In 2024-26, 6.3% of expected onsides were recovered (3.2-11.9, n=127).
method: An onside is a kickoff described as onside. Expected means Q4 with the kicking team trailing, and surprise is all the others. WPA is compared with normal Q1-Q3 kickoffs within 14 points, with game bootstrap CIs. Teams pick their spots, so the rates are upper bounds.
data: nflverse play-by-play, 2015 to 2026 wk 8, 691 onside kicks.
split_check: Surprise recovery was 28% in 2015-18 (n=32) and 21% in 2019-23 (n=24). Expected stays near 9%.
